To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the protein component(s) that interacts with signal sequence of precursor proteins destined for chloroplast or mitochondria.

the signal peptide of precursor proteins is recognized by a protein receptor in the outer membrane of the chloroplast and mitochondrial envelopes, that the receptor protein is localized in the contact sites between the outer and the inner envelope membrane, and that it is a component of the protein import machinery.

1) the import receptor(s) is a contact site protein(s) of the envelope of chloroplasts or mitochondria; 2) the import receptor of chloroplasts is a peripheral protein of the outer envelope membrane; and 3) the import receptor is a protein of the outer membrane of mitochondria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for targeting of proteins to chloroplasts and/or mitochondria, with a particular emphasis on the identification and characterization of receptor(s).
the identification and characterization of the protein import receptor(s) in chloroplasts and in mitochondria.
the elucidation of the mechanism(s) of protein import into the chloroplast and mitochondrial compartments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the import of proteins into mitochondria and chloroplasts is mediated by a receptor system.
a receptor exists for the protein import into chlor- and mitochondria, and that it is a protein of the outer membrane of the respective organelle.
the receptor(s) is a component of the contact sites between the outer and the inner membrane of chloroplastic envelope or of mitochondrion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the protein component(s) of the outer membrane of the chloroplast envelope which interacts with the chloroplast transit peptide.
the signal sequence is the recognition site for the receptor, and that the receptor is located in the outer membrane of the organelles.
the import receptor is a membrane protein, located in the outer membrane of chloroplast and mitochondrial envelope, and that it is a component of "contact sites" in these organelles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a common import machinery between chloroplasts and mitochondrial.
the import receptor(s) is an essential component of a protein import system.
the import of proteins into organelles is mediated by a receptor-mediated pathway.
